title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election for New York's 5th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for New York's 5th Congressional District in Southeast Queens pits 28-year incumbent Gregory Meeks against Republican challengers in what is rated a safely Democratic seat (Cook PVI D+24). Meeks, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, is the presumptive Democratic nominee after primary challenger Salvatore Padellaro was disqualified. The Republican primary features three candidates—George Marsh, Alexandria Foxworth, and Aaron Cherry—seeking to challenge Meeks in the general election. The district, which includes Jamaica, Hollis, Laurelton, Richmond Hill, Ozone Park, Howard Beach, and the Rockaways, has not elected a Republican since the 1990s.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for this race. The district is heavily Democratic (Cook PVI D+24), and Meeks won the 2024 general election with 72.9% of the vote.

candidates.name: Gregory Meeks
candidates.summary: Gregory W. Meeks has represented New York's 5th Congressional District since 1998 and chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee. A former New York State Assembly member and Queens assistant district attorney, Meeks is a senior member of the Congressional Black Caucus and has built a reputation on foreign policy and economic development issues. He is running for a fifteenth full term in 2026.
